history.period: Built 1527 CE by Emperor Babur; Humayun's platform addition 16th century
history.summary: IMPORTANT: THIS IS A MUSLIM MOSQUE, NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - keep-or-drop decision needed for this dataset. The Kabuli Bagh Mosque (with the domed structure called the 'Tomb' in this row's name) is in Kabuli Bagh Colony, Panipat, about 2 km from the city centre. It was built in 1527 by the Mughal emperor Babur to commemorate his victory over Sultan Ibrahim Lodi at the First Battle of Panipat (1526) - it is among the oldest surviving Mughal monuments in India and, per some sources, the first Mughal monument in the country. Babur named it after his wife Mussamat Kabuli Begum. Its architecture reflects the royal mosques of Samarkand and Ferghana: brick and red sandstone with stucco plaster, Persian inscriptions (dated 1527), an entrance gate with hemispherical dome, octagonal corner towers, and a prayer hall with a large central dome; a water tank in the complex is also attributed to Babur. A few years later Humayun added a masonry platform, the 'Chabutra Fateh Mubarak', to mark his victory over Sher Shah's forces near Panipat (per one source dated '934 Hijri (A.D.1557)' - that Hijri year converts to 1527-28 CE, so the dating is inconsistent; flagged unresolved). CONFLICTS: sources agree on Babur 1527; one source calls it the 'first Mughal monument in India'. The mosque has been closed to prayers and sealed since 1992 (after the Babri Masjid demolition), and its premises are in ruins with one wing partially collapsed. The word 'Tomb' in the row name follows the source terminology; no separate burial monument is clearly documented - it appears to refer to the mosque's hemispherical domed hall.

name: Kabuli Bagh Mosque and Tomb
town_description: Panipat is a historic city in Haryana on NH-44 (G.T. Road), about 90 km north of Delhi. It is famous as the site of the three battles of Panipat (1526, 1556, 1761) and is today India's 'Textile City' and 'City of Weavers', the biggest centre for quality blankets and carpets.
